_readme: The known-good catalog (src/catalog.js): per game exe, the setup PROVEN to run DLSS 5 and the setups known to be dead ends, each with its source. Only real evidence goes here -- a confirmed run on a real install, or a run log -- never a guess. After any edit run `node tools/catalog/build.js`: it checks every entry and rewrites sha256, and the app refuses the file while the hash does not match. `node tools/catalog/build.js --digest <issue body> --source "issue #N" --write` adds a report from an issue's Run digest.

entries.notes: 32-bit DirectX 9 on dgVoodoo2. The 00BE89B7 crash and the black screen were both this app writing ColorSpace=argb8888_srgb, which dgVoodoo rejects -- and a rejected value voids the rest of the config, so VRAM stayed at the 256MB default until the game ran out and CreateTexture returned NULL. Fixed 2026-09-21. This game is left in exclusive fullscreen (the forced-borderless keys black-screen it), so it runs with host_window=3 and cast_mode=1 and the panel opens on Alt+Home. It still dies on focus loss (a game bug).
sources: live test 2026-09-21: 600+ DLSS 5 frames at 56.6 fps, clean exit, panel confirmed

entries.name: Fallout: New Vegas
entries.notes: 32-bit DirectX 9 on dgVoodoo2. It crashed on every world load until the app started naming the real GPU vendor to the game (dgVoodoo.conf [DirectXExt] AdapterIDType, app v2.3.16): without it the game does not recognise the adapter, falls back to its Shader Model 2.0 path (RendererInfo.txt: RenderPath BSSM_SV_2_0, Shader Package 2) and then dereferences the NULL that BSShaderManager::GetShader(29) returns, at FalloutNV+0x757aa9. Its own caps were never the problem -- RendererInfo.txt reports "3.0 Support: yes" one line above "3.0 Lighting: no". An install made before v2.3.16 gets the key on sync. FalloutNV.exe is not large-address-aware, so it is still capped at 2 GB; the 4GB patch is worth having but was not needed for this.
sources: live test 2026-09-21: crash reproduced twice at FalloutNV+0x757aa9 (dlss5-feed-crash.dmp, cdb), fixed by AdapterIDType and confirmed by the user
local runs 2026-09-21 (nr-ran x3): feeder32 via dgvoodoo, dx9

entries.name: Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne

dead_ends.why: dgVoodoo2 creates its Direct3D 11 device past ReShade's hooks, so ReShade never draws and the Feeder has no frames
dead_ends.source: live test 2026-09-23/24: ReShade.log hooked d3d11/dxgi, no device or swapchain from dgVoodoo after the game started

entries.notes: 32-bit Direct3D 8 (MAX-FX, rendering through e2driver\e2_d3d8_driver_mfc.dll) on DXVK, with ReShade as its 32-bit Vulkan layer. Its startup DxDiag probe loads Windows' own d3d8/d3d9 first, so DXVK only loads under renamed names: the renderer is pointed at dgd8.dll (DXVK's d3d8, itself pointed at dgd9.dll = DXVK's d3d9); the upper-case D3D8.DLL, its DirectX version check, is left alone. It minimises on focus loss, so the DLSS 5 panel is drawn in-game (host_window=3, cast_mode=1) and AllowTaskSwitching is set.
sources: live test 2026-09-24: host64\OptiScaler.log, 4,500 DLSS 5 frames (0 model failures) at ~62 fps; ReShade Vulkan layer; in-game panel confirmed
